forum.title: Option for ADC3 Differential input is missing in CubeMX
forum.best_answer_content:
ADC3 Channel 1 differential mode uses ADC3\_IN1 as the positive input and ADC3\_IN2 as the negative input.

![Screenshot 2026-03-17 120904.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/82d31cae-9ad8-62f4-9a53-96cadcc7a28e.png "Screenshot 2026-03-17 120904.png")

The ADC3\_IN2 pin isn't broken out on the LQFP64 package, so differential mode for ADC3 channel 1 is not available.

![Screenshot 2026-03-17 120621.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/3a46cd06-7f6a-d1a8-5106-1162a777c45e.png "Screenshot 2026-03-17 120621.png")
forum.content_text: I am setting up my STM32F303RET6 for four differential inputs to be sampled simultaneously. As seen in the screenshot attached. there is no option for differential inputs on CubeMX. Am I missing something here? I have reset whole project to ensure no pins are assigned elsewhere.
forum.author: Ankurgupta4u

scraped_replies.html:
Welcome @Ankurgupta4u, to the community!

The STM32F303RET6 has a 100-pin package, so the differential mode cannot be implemented for all ADC channels. With the STM32F303VET6 in the 144-pin package, you can indeed select the differential mode for ADC3 IN1.

Does it answer your question?

Regards
/Peter
scraped_replies.author: Peter BENSCH

scraped_replies.html:
ADC3 Channel 1 differential mode uses ADC3_IN1 as the positive input and ADC3_IN2 as the negative input.

The ADC3_IN2 pin isn't broken out on the LQFP64 package, so differential mode for ADC3 channel 1 is not available.
scraped_replies.author: TDK

scraped_replies.html:
Thank you both, I have been trying to use PB0 and PB1 as differential inputs for ADC3 and had to install CubeMX since there are multiple docuements to refer. I still think it is a strange design choice. But I am able to configure OpAmp3 on PB0 and PB1 and direct the output to ADC3, which should address it without requiring design changes thankfully.

I would appreciate your advice about this approach.
